topic: Does the order of few-shot examples change the accuracy of a language model on text classification?

review.Summary: This paper investigates whether the order of few-shot examples affects the accuracy of a language model in text classification. The experiment uses a local model via Ollama with the IMDb dataset, permuting few-shot examples to assess their impact on classification performance. Despite the structured design, the results show an accuracy of 0.00, suggesting the model failed to produce valid classifications.
Strengths: Use of a local language model for fast execution
Repetition of the experiment for statistical significance
Weaknesses: Results show 0.00 accuracy, which lacks empirical support for the hypothesis
Lack of detailed analysis of model outputs (e.g., why no valid classifications were produced)
Insufficient discussion on the model's failure to interpret prompts or examples
Minimal data and test examples may not be sufficient for reliable conclusions
No comparison with baselines or alternative prompt formats
Questions: Why did the model fail to produce any valid classifications? What aspects of the prompt or model setup may have contributed to this?
Were the test examples properly labeled and formatted for the model to understand the task?
What is the role of the few-shot examples in the prompt, and why did their order not influence the model's output?
Limitations: Model may not be capable of few-shot learning with the current setup
Insufficient data and test examples may limit generalizability
No baseline comparisons or alternative prompt formats were tested
Lack of detailed model output analysis
